title: ESP32 OTA: partitions and recovery from a failed update

questions.prompt: Which option states the main idea of “ESP32 OTA: partitions and recovery from a failed update” correctly?
options: OTA (Over-The-Air) updates a device over a network instead of plugging in a USB cable.
For safer ESP32 updates, flash can hold the running application and another app slot.
This example uploads from Arduino IDE to a supported ESP32 on the same Wi-Fi network.
questions.answer: For safer ESP32 updates, flash can hold the running application and another app slot.
questions.explanation: For safer ESP32 updates, flash can hold the running application and another app slot.

questions.prompt: Which additional fact about “ESP32 OTA: partitions and recovery from a failed update” is accurate?
options: updating hundreds at once is risky.
For example, new firmware can be sent over Wi-Fi to a greenhouse sensor.
The new image is written to the inactive slot
The first setup still needs USB: install a sketch with Wi-Fi and OTA support over the cable, then later uploads can use the network.
questions.answer: The new image is written to the inactive slot
questions.explanation: The new image is written to the inactive slot

questions.prompt: Which practical detail should be considered when using “ESP32 OTA: partitions and recovery from a failed update”?
options: after reboot, the device performs basic health checks.

OTA makes remote maintenance easier, but the device needs a safe recovery path if power or connectivity fails.
